item.title: Ladies hold on to defeat Fruitland
item.description: Holy smokes what a game! Weiser hosted Fruitland on Tuesday, Jan. 27. Fruitland had previously defeated Weiser by nine points on a late run in the fourth quarter of that game. It almost happened again but Weiser had built a large enough lead and hit just enough baskets to keep afloat. The assists on the night were many and showed the teamwork these Ladies have striven for. item.title: Weiser gives the Vandals a close game
item.description: Wolverine Zayn Crossley led Weiser with 18 points in a Saturday battle with the McCall Vandals. Photo by Nancy Grindstaff The McCall Vandals came to Weiser on Saturday, Jan. 31, to start the second half of conference play. The frosh/soph won 59-24 and the JV also won 63-30. The varsity had a hard time in McCall when these two teams first met. This game was a lot closer and Weiser played a lot better. item.title: Weiser dominates the Pirates in conference win
item.description: The Wolverines closed out the first half of conference play with a 65-21 win over the Payette Pirates on Thursday, Jan. 29. Pictured at right, Weiser senior Shayd Crossley gets his hand on the tip off at the start of the match up. Photo by David Lukens This was the last game of the first round of conference for the Weiser Wolverines. The setting: the dome in Payette. The day: Thursday, Jan 29. The outcome: a smashing win 65-21. Everyone played in this game. The JV was also a monstrous win 69-4.

item.description: The Lady Wolverines put up three big wins over Payette on Friday, Jan. 30. WHS senior Porter Hart goes up for a two-point basket in the first half. item.title: Power rate study up first, solar tabled
item.description: The Weiser City Council put a proposal to study adding solar power to the local grid on ice in favor of first determining what residents can expect to pay for power in the future. A rate analysis would have been part of the broader solar feasibility study, but the council voted unanimously to table solar research, balking at the price, in favor of taking up a power price study at a future meeting.
